_comment: Bilinear interpolation over a takeoff performance grid. The GRID VALUES in src/performance/*.json are unverified and gated; the MATH here is what these fixtures pin. Expectations are hand-computed from the corners so a regression in the interpolation cannot hide behind plausible-looking output. Grid used is the C172S table: grid[pressureAltFt][tempC] = [groundRoll, over50ft].

interpolation.why: exact grid point must return the published cell untouched
top corner of the envelope is still inside it
midway between 0 and 2000 ft at a published temp: (925+1105)/2, (1685+2035)/2
midway between 10C and 20C at sea level: (860+925)/2 rounds to 893, (1570+1685)/2 to 1628

true bilinear with NO intermediate rounding. Corners 860/925/1025/1105 give 892.5 then 1065, then 978.75 -> 979. Rounding the 892.5 first yields 980, which is what a naive two-step implementation produces - that one-foot gap is the whole point of this case.
above the published envelope — must report nothing, NEVER extrapolate past where the manufacturer stopped testing
hotter than the published table; extrapolating here would understate the distance on exactly the day it matters
below the table; a below-sea-level field is outside published data
colder than the table — outside is outside, even when the answer would be conservative

corrections.why: no wind leaves the figures alone
TAILWIND. 2 kt increases distances 10 percent — must never be treated as a small headwind benefit
dry grass adds 15 percent OF THE GROUND ROLL to both figures, not 15 percent of each
